_about: Machine-readable manifest of upstream PyTorch tests that are FUNDAMENTALLY inapplicable to the reduced, CPU-only, single-threaded wasm32-emscripten torch build packaged by this prototype. Consumed by conftest.py. Each category is either environment-gated (applies only under the wasm runtime, key `wasm_only: true`) or always-inapplicable. Skips here are inapplicability-by-environment ONLY; genuine reduced-build failures are tracked separately in logs/known_failures.md and are NOT listed here.
_build_config: USE_CUDA/ROCM/XPU=0, USE_MKLDNN/FBGEMM/NNPACK/QNNPACK/PYTORCH_QNNPACK/XNNPACK=0, USE_DISTRIBUTED/TENSORPIPE/GLOO/MPI=0, USE_OPENMP=0 (ATEN_THREADING=NATIVE, single-threaded), USE_NUMPY=0, USE_KINETO=0, USE_ITT=0, USE_MIMALLOC=0, USE_ONNX=0, BUILD_CAFFE2=0. Runtime: xeus-python wasm32 in the browser, single process, no fork/exec/threads, no host compiler, sandboxed FS.

categories.reason: No GPU/accelerator backend in wasm; build is USE_CUDA/ROCM/XPU=0. CUDA/MPS/XPU device variants are not even instantiated on a CPU-only runtime, but some tests hardcode accelerator use or gate on multi-GPU.
Build is USE_DISTRIBUTED/TENSORPIPE/GLOO/MPI=0; torch.distributed / RPC / c10d process groups are unavailable and the single wasm process cannot form a group.
The wasm runtime is a single process with no fork()/exec()/subprocess and no _multiprocessing/shared-memory manager; tests that spawn processes or shell out cannot run.

Build is single-threaded (USE_OPENMP=0, ATEN_THREADING=NATIVE); wasm has no host threads/thread-pool. Tests asserting multi-thread parallelism, thread-count>1, or thread-safety races are inapplicable.
MKLDNN/oneDNN, FBGEMM, NNPACK, QNNPACK, PYTORCH_QNNPACK, XNNPACK and the quantized engines are all compiled out (USE_*=0); no quantized engine is registered.
No host C/C++ compiler at runtime in wasm; torch.utils.cpp_extension (load/load_inline), TorchInductor/torch.compile codegen, and NVRTC/Triton compilation cannot run.
torch built with USE_NUMPY=0: the C++ numpy bridge is absent, so torch.from_numpy / Tensor.numpy() / numpy-array interop raise even though the numpy Python package is importable.
The wasm runtime has a sandboxed in-memory FS with no real mmap, file locking, signals, or OS-level paths; tests depending on these OS facilities are inapplicable.
Tests marked slow or allocating very large tensors OOM the constrained wasm heap or exceed the interactive time budget; not a correctness signal for the reduced build.
USE_KINETO=0 and USE_ITT=0: the profiler backend and ITT annotations are not built.
